kpis.description: A new authenticated user pastes a repo URL and reaches a fully scored ScanReport — the maturity level, radar, and roadmap all rendered — within their first session. Measured as the share of new sign-ups who hit this state within 7 days of account creation.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"In Posthog (or equivalent), compute: users who fired `scan_completed` within 7 days of `user_signed_up` ÷ total `user_signed_up` events in the same cohort window. Express as a percentage."}
kpis.name: First-scan activation rate
kpis.rationale: The entire product value chain starts here — if a new user never reaches a scored report, every downstream metric (retention, conversion, fleet depth) is moot.

kpis.description: Share of repos (or orgs) that receive a second or later scan within 30 days of their first completed scan. A second scan is the clearest signal that a user acted on the roadmap and returned to measure progress.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"Query: repos with ≥2 `scan_completed` events whose second event falls within 30 days of the first, divided by all repos with at least one `scan_completed` event."}
kpis.name: 30-day re-scan rate
kpis.rationale: Re-scan is the product's core loop — maturity only moves if teams act, re-measure, and iterate; a low rate signals the roadmap is not driving real engineering change.

kpis.description: Percentage of users who start on the free tier (≤5 scans/month) and upgrade to Pro or Team within 30 days of their first completed scan.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"In Polar's dashboard, count subscriptions created where the customer previously held a free plan, divided by all free users who completed at least one scan in the same cohort. Or pull subscription events from the Polar webhook log stored in Supabase and match against first-scan timestamps."}
kpis.name: Free-to-paid conversion (30-day)
kpis.rationale: Conversion from free to paid is the primary revenue gate; watching it weekly reveals whether scan value is legible enough to justify $10 before users exhaust their 5-scan allowance.

kpis.description: Among orgs with an active GitHub App installation, the percentage that have scanned at least 3 repositories. A single-repo scan is a trial; scanning a fleet is adoption.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"Count GitHub App installations where the associated org has ≥3 distinct repos with a completed scan in the last 30 days, divided by total active installations. Cross-reference Supabase org membership records with the scan DB."}
kpis.name: Org fleet scan depth
kpis.rationale: Fleet depth separates trial users from genuine adopters and is the leading signal for Team/Enterprise upgrade potential — a shallow fleet means the org-dashboard and fleet-rollup features are invisible to the user.

kpis.description: Share of completed scan reports where at least one prioritised roadmap recommendation is accepted or marked in-progress by the org within 14 days of the report being delivered.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"Query the recommendation-status table for rows where `status IN (accepted, in_progress, completed)` and the status change occurred within 14 days of the parent scan's `completed_at`. Divide by total scans delivered in the same window."}
kpis.name: Roadmap engagement rate
kpis.rationale: The roadmap is the product's promise of outcome — if no one acts on it, Ascent is an expensive vanity mirror rather than a change engine, and churn follows.

kpis.description: Count of distinct organisations (or individual accounts on the free tier) that initiate at least one scan in a rolling 7-day window. Primary pulse metric for product health.
kpis.measure_config: {"connector":"supabase","instruction":"Count distinct org_id values in the Supabase `scan_events` or equivalent table where `initiated_at` falls within the last 7 days and `status != cancelled`. Reduces to a single integer."}
kpis.name: Weekly active scanning orgs
kpis.rationale: Weekly active orgs is the one number that collapses activation, retention, and fleet growth into a single weekly heartbeat the team can act on immediately.

kpis.description: Percentage of initiated scans that terminate in a pipeline error (LLM timeout, GitHub 403/rate-limit, unhandled exception) rather than a completed or user-cancelled state. Tracked via Sentry error volume against total scan initiations.
kpis.measure_config: {"connector":"sentry","instruction":"Fetch the count of issues tagged `scan_pipeline` in the last 7 days from Sentry. Divide by total scan initiations from the application DB or a Sentry custom metric counter for the same window. Return as a percentage."}
kpis.name: Scan pipeline error rate
kpis.rationale: A pipeline failure is invisible to the user (they see a spinner, then an error) and silently consumes quota and LLM credits — even a 5% error rate erodes trust and unit economics faster than any feature gap.

kpis.description: Mean token spend in USD (across all configured providers: Gemini, Bedrock, OpenAI, Claude CLI) per scan that reaches a ScanReport. Directly determines the unit economics of every metered and unlimited-plan scan.
kpis.measure_config: {"instruction":"From the LightTrack OTLP spans (local :8787 instance or exported trace store), aggregate `llm.usage.cost` across all spans with `scan_id` set, group by `scan_id`, and compute the mean over the last 7 days. If LightTrack is not exporting to a queryable store, pull total token counts from provider dashboards and apply the per-model cost schedule in `src/lib/llm/`."}
kpis.name: Average LLM cost per completed scan
kpis.rationale: The LLM call is ~99% of scan wall-time and 100% of scan COGS; an unbounded cost-per-scan that creeps above the credit price makes every scan economically underwater regardless of plan tier.
